note: Window agent p1610-p1619, 2 Nov 2026. Corrections: Swedish Ingria drawn as the whole of Leningrad oblast in 1617-1618 (events/0 + keyframe_overrides/0); Bikaner's centre held by the Mughals (events/1); Russia's Chernigov-Severia cession drawn as all of Kursk and Bryansk too (events/2-3, same keyframe override); Ottoman Iraq dropped in 1612 without an event (keyframe_overrides/1, which holds to 1625). Not patched: Denmark-Norway as a vassal of Holstein (duchy-of-holstein ledger/3), already closed by p1500-p1599 events/0 in 1526; the Ming/Tumed overlap of 1619, already settled for Shanxi by p1600-p1609 rulings/0 (the conflict falls from 134 to 32 cells).

region.text: the part of the gazetteer's Ingria (all of Leningrad oblast, 388 cells) that lies outside Cliopatria's Swedish shape of 1619 (95 cells): Tikhvin, Ladoga, Lodeynoye Pole and the east of the oblast

events.note: 9 March 1617, Stolbovo: 'Sweden gained the province of Kexholm in Karelia and the province of Ingria - including the fortress of Nöteborg'; 'Novgorod and other Swedish territorial gains during the war would be returned to Russia'. The dossier's Ingria region is the whole oblast, far wider than the province; Cliopatria's Swedish 1619 shape (95 Ingria cells, 24,000 km2) is the extent of record, and the rest of the oblast goes back to Russia.

region.text: the Bikaner State of about 60,000 km2, whose centre (97 cells round the city) the draft gives to the Mughal Empire

events.note: Bikaner stayed its own state under Mughal suzerainty: 'The state of Bikaner was founded in 1465'; its rulers acknowledged Akbar's suzerainty (Kalyan Mal, 1542-1571) and served as Mughal generals (Rai Singh, 1571-1612). The page records no annexation or occupation of any part of Bikaner before 1700, so the Mughal-owned hole in the middle of its disc returns to Bikaner.

region.text: the part of the gazetteer's Chernigov region (417 cells, with all of Kursk and most of Bryansk oblast) that lies outside Cliopatria's Commonwealth shape of 1619

events.note: Truce of Deulino, 11 December 1618: the Commonwealth got 'the territories of Chernigov and Severia (Siewiersk) and the city of Smolensk'. The dossier's Chernigov region (Bryansk, Chernihiv and Kursk) is wider than the Chernihiv voivodeship and Severia; Cliopatria's Commonwealth shape of 1619 is the extent of record (186 of its cells), so the rest (Kursk and most of Bryansk, about 216 cells) stays Russian instead of passing to the Commonwealth for one year and coming back in the 1619 snap.

region.text: the part of the gazetteer's Chernigov region outside Cliopatria's Commonwealth shape of 1619 (Kursk and most of Bryansk oblast)

events.note: 4 January 1619: the Truce of Deulino 'was signed in the village of Deulino on 11 December 1618 and took effect on 4 January 1619'; 'The Commonwealth gained control over the Smolensk and Chernihiv Voivodeships' (the page names neither Kursk nor Bryansk). Companion of events/2: the dossier's own gain of 1619/1 (ledger/20) takes the whole gazetteer Chernigov region, so the part outside Cliopatria's 1619 Commonwealth shape (about 216 cells, Kursk and most of Bryansk) is handed back to Russia in the same month. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: source changed from the Polish-Russian War (1609-1618) page, which has no 'took effect' or 4 January date, to the Truce of Deulino page, which has both.]

correction.text: the 1612 shape minus Ingria as Sweden held it (Cliopatria's Swedish 1619 shape inside the Ingria region), Kexholm (Stolbovo, March 1617) and Chernigov-Severia as the Commonwealth held it (Deulino, December 1618: Cliopatria's Commonwealth shape of 1619 inside the Chernigov region)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier cuts the whole gazetteer Ingria region (all of Leningrad oblast, 388 cells) from Russia in 1617-1618, though Stolbovo gave Sweden 'the province of Ingria - including the fortress of Nöteborg' and Kexholm and returned 'Novgorod and other Swedish territorial gains'. The Chernigov region is narrowed the same way (Kursk and most of Bryansk stay Russian). Narrowed to the Cliopatria Swedish shape so that Russia keeps the east of the oblast; matches swedish-empire events/0 and removes the 1619 snap (245 cells back to Russia).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1612 shape plus the whole of Iraq, Ottoman until the Safavid capture of Baghdad on 14 January 1624

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own 1609 keyframe and its 1624-1625 ledger losses treat all of country Iraq as Ottoman until 1624, but the unchanged 1612 shape lacks the western desert (Al-Anbar, Al-Muthannia, An-Najaf: about 795 cells), which drops out in 1612 with no event. The page: Baghdad fell to the Safavids on 14 January 1624 ('took it on 14 January 1624'), Basra was still Ottoman in 1624, and 'the Persians soon captured most of Iraq, including ... Kirkuk and Mosul and the Shia holy shrines of Najaf and Karbala'.

correction.text: the 1612 shape without the province of Kandahar until 22 June 1622; from then the shape as drawn; also without Iraq, which was Ottoman from the Peace of Amasya (1555) to Shah Abbas's capture of Baghdad on 14 January 1624; plus Armavir, Ararat and Aragatsotn (the Yerevan area, Erivan Province) and West Azarbaijan, which the ledger gave the Safavids (Tabriz 1603, Yerevan 1604, the rest of Azerbaijan 1612) and the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha left them, but Cliopatria's 1612 shape leaves to the Ottomans

keyframe_overrides.why: Seam sm-04, from the p1600-p1609 report: the 1612 snaps leave the Caucasus right (the 97 contested Armenian and Azerbaijani cells pass to the Safavids when the contest ends) but strip a frontier strip to nobody for 1612-1625: 15 Armenian cells and 63 of West Azarbaijan's 147 cells (44.1-45.2 E, 37.2-39.7 N), which the Ottoman 1612 shape does not claim either. The page: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (20 November 1612) 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya', and the Safavids regained 'the territories ceded in 1590 to the Ottomans; Azerbaijan, Georgia, Erivan Province, Daghestan, Shirvan, Karabakh, Lorestan, and Khuzestan'; the Peace of Amasya page has 'the Persians retained their former capital Tabriz' and the frontier run 'via the western slopes of the Zagros Mountains'. The correction adds the two regions to the dossier's own shape. Not added, pages silent: 30 Turkish cells at the Ararat end (43.4-44.5 E, 39.4-40.7 N) and 32 Kuwait cells the 1612 shape also drops. [Review sm-04, 3 Nov 2026: replaced by a corrected entry. The dossier's own safavid-dynasty_1612 correction was edited at 23:56 on 2 Nov (fx-44, R058), after this entry, and now adds Armavir, Ararat, Aragatsotn (Erivan Province) and all of West Azarbaijan itself. Against it the entry's whole country of Armenia added only 7 cells of Shirak, which the Ottoman 1612 shape claims and which the dossier leaves out on purpose ('advanced towards Kars' only; the Peace of Amasya page: 'Kars was declared neutral'); the pages name Erivan Province, not Shirak. The correction is now the dossier's own, verbatim, so the entry changes nothing; it can be deleted (it is the last keyframe override of this file) so that later dossier edits of this shape are not masked.]
